attributes.label: Adversarial Agent Pattern
attributes.original_attribution_passages: ["\\paragraph{Context.} A specification has been approved and an agent (or chain of agents) has begun executing it. The specification is the authoritative source of truth, but the act of execution---turning prose into code, tests, configurations---introduces interpretive freedom. Whoever does the building also has the strongest incentive to declare the work done.", "\\paragraph{Problem.} A single agent that both implements and verifies its own output is structurally biased toward declaring success. Self-verifying agents rationalise away gaps between the artifact and the spec, hallucinate the existence of behaviours they did not implement, and---most diagnostically---``just change the test'' when the code under construction cannot be made to pass. Kent Beck identifies this as the dominant LLM failure mode in test-first workflows: the model treats the test as another mutable artifact rather than as the contract the code must satisfy. Without an external check whose incentive is inverted, errors compound silently across phases.", "  \\node[pcin] (spec) {SPEC\\\\(source of truth)};", "\\paragraph{Consequences.} \\emph{Benefits.} Hallucinated completions are caught at the role boundary rather than after merge. The read-only sandbox makes ``just change the test'' architecturally impossible: the Verifier has no write privilege over the artifact under audit. Failure feedback is structured (spec~$\\to$~Coordinator) rather than ad hoc, which keeps the spec the single source of truth and prevents the Implementor and Verifier from negotiating their way to a passing build. The pattern composes cleanly with gate enforcement (Pattern~C1) because the Verifier's verdict is the natural input to Gate~3 (verification gate). \\emph{Trade-offs.} Inference cost roughly doubles per task because the Verifier re-reads the spec independently. Latency increases because verification cannot be parallelised with implementation without losing the inverted incentive (a Verifier that watches the Implementor work is no longer adversarial). Coordinator design becomes the highest-leverage decision: a weak Coordinator that decomposes badly will produce both bad implementations and irrelevant verifications."]
attributes.limitation: Attribution retained as written in the supplied source, not independently verified inventorship.

attributes.label: Evidence-Pack Provenance
attributes.original_attribution_passages: ["%  Sources: Ralph Copilot's per-cycle documentation model.]", "\\paragraph{Solution.} Every autonomous cycle produces a structured \\textbf{evidence pack}\\,---\\,three artifacts at minimum, written to a per-cycle directory under \\code{.specify/evidence/}. The \\code{prompt.md} captures the exact input the agent received: the spec excerpt, the constitution sections, the prior artifacts, the task statement. The \\code{result.md} captures what the agent did: the diff, the test results, the tools invoked, the decisions made and their rationale. The \\code{verdict.md} captures the agent's self-assessment: did the cycle meet the acceptance criteria? Which evidence supports that claim? Which open questions remain? The pack is committed to the repository (it is part of the source of truth, not a transient log) and is linked from \\code{tasks.md} so the trail from item to cycle to evidence is one click."]

attributes.label: Escalation Protocol
attributes.original_attribution_passages: ["%  Sources: BMAD's explicit handoff protocol; AI-RPI's escalation model.]", "\\paragraph{A1 --- Constitution-Driven Development.} Enterprise SDD generates the constitution through the \\code{@constitution} agent during \\code{sdd init}; the output lives in \\code{.specify/memory/constitution.md} and is loaded by every agent's reading procedure. Update before the first feature, then amend explicitly through a dedicated PR with team sign-off; never edit the constitution as a side effect of a feature PR. Adapted from Spec Kit's constitutional governance and Karpathy's \\code{CLAUDE.md} discipline.", "\\paragraph{A2 --- Clarify Before Plan.} Enterprise SDD wires this into Phase~1.3: \\code{@clarification} runs after \\code{@requirement-analyst} and before Gate~1. The P1/P2/P3 tiering uses the same priority taxonomy as the runtime escalation protocol (Pattern~D4), so the team learns one vocabulary for ``how blocking is this?'' Adapted from Spec Kit's \\code{/clarify} template and the \\code{CLARIFY\\_BEFORE\\_PLAN} rule first articulated in GSD.", "\\paragraph{A3 --- Progressive Specification.} Enterprise SDD's \\code{sdd new --progressive} mode marks the spec with the progressive flag and requires every Gate~1 check to compare the current spec against the previous iteration\\,---\\,if no \\code{[NEEDS-CLARIFICATION]} markers were resolved, the gate fails. Use only on well-understood feature \\emph{types} (UI iterations, integration extensions); set an iteration budget (typically 3) and treat budget exhaustion as the trigger to elevate the feature back to standard pipeline. Adapted from Spec Loop Engine's iterative refinement model.", "\\paragraph{A4 --- Red-Team Specification.} Run \\code{sdd skill run red-team-spec <feature-id>} after the author has self-reviewed and before Gate~1 is requested. The skill's instruction explicitly forbids the agent from confirming what the spec does well; its only output is failure modes. Findings flow into the same gap-closure analysis (Pattern~A5) used for traceability. The pattern is one of three Enterprise~SDD mechanisms that implement the inverted-incentive principle from the Adversarial Agent Pattern (C5). Adapted from security red-teaming practice.", "\\paragraph{A5 --- Gap-Closure Analysis.} Run \\code{sdd analyze --gaps} on brownfield projects after \\code{sdd ingest} has imported the existing repository structure. Use the prioritised orphan list to drive a small allocation of each sprint to retroactive specification (typically 10--20\\,\\%); resist the temptation to declare a ``spec sprint'' that pauses feature delivery, which historically produces specs nobody references. Adapted from AI-RPI Protocol's traceability model.", "\\paragraph{B3 --- Anti-Sycophancy Enforcement.} Enterprise SDD ships the rule as part of the shared \\code{all-agents.instructions.md} so that every agent inherits the same wording; individual agents may extend the rule but cannot weaken it.
